text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3cfe245ae5f381fcad84cc3889ee3d3b as of 2026-09-02T23:11:16.129Z: {"title":"Jeremy Caradonna · Council · inc"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🧩"} **Filled card. Not published.** Jeremy Caradonna · Council · incumbent (2022–26 City term). Re-scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)**, 12-topic template, Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom and is Joa's to apply or reject. Alignment compute APPLIED letter stays **—**. **What changed from the first pass.** The first pass recorded "no readable 2026 Plan text" and scored 5 of 55. That premise was wrong. The Platform, Achievements and Future Focus accordions are **Elfsight widgets injected by JavaScript** — absent from the WordPress HTML, present in the widget payload. The full text was retrieved and independently re-verified against the widget's own data endpoint on 2026-09-02. It is a **10-section platform of roughly 70 written commitments** plus a 10-section record claim. Scored answers move 5 → 30. ## Card
Field Value
Name Jeremy Caradonna
Office Council (also seeking CRD Director)
Kind inc (2022–26 City term — sourced miss caps the cell below Close; non-contradicting Record = 📋, not in n)
Platform URL (2026) [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · home [https://www.electjeremy.ca/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/)
Platform lastmod Page shell 2026-05-21 (WordPress modified_gmt); home 2026-08-04; endorsements 2026-08-28. **Accordion text is Elfsight-hosted and carries no timestamp — lastmod unknown.** No sitemap (/sitemap.xml and /wp-sitemap.xml both 404).
Retrieved 2026-09-02

Record lines 📋 (shown, not scored) **5** (rows 12, 14, 29, 50, 55) — not in n
Letter (only at 5 scored answers: B+, B, C, D, or —) **—** · awaiting Joa's click. Internal proposal at the bottom of this page. Alignment compute APPLIED stays **—**.
Nomination status **Not filed as of 2026-09-02.** City lists Alto and Atkinson (mayor) and Gardiner (council). Nominations close **11 Sep 2026, 4pm**. Announced intent 19 Dec 2025.
Checked by · date Verifier · 2026-09-02 (re-score)
### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **said** "Keep property taxes at reasonable rates, while managing inflation." No cap, no formula, no number, no supermajority rule. Term record: 3.2% (2023), 7.93% (2024), 8.68% (2025), 7.28% overall / **9.34% residential** (2026). His site claims the term kept increases "in the bottom half of regional municipalities." [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [vicnews](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02 / vote 7 May 2026
Downtown order M26 / M27 **said** "Work with VicPD, Bylaw, the Province, and service providers to limit and restrict open drug consumption and to reduce street disorder." No Public Order Team, no unified command, no 6am–10pm bylaw hours, no staffing number. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
Housing M6 **said** "Make Victoria attractive to families - develop and expand the Family Housing Regulation (requiring multi-bedroom homes in new builds)." A composition instrument. No unit total, no 25/20/15/30 mix, no quarterly composition reporting. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
Household bill M66d **—** Water, sewer, stormwater and a combined household number appear nowhere on the 2026 site. The word "budget" appears only inside "on time and on budget." — —
Written program — **yes** Authorized 2026 site with a 10-section platform (\~70 commitments), a 10-section Achievements record, a stated objective, endorsements and videos. Not costed, no dates, no service standards, no numbers except canopy 40% and CRHC 3,000–3,500. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod 2026-05-21 (shell), retrieved 2026-09-02
--- ## The 12 topics Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date**. Rules as written on the template page. A dash is unknown, not a fail. No topic gets its own letter. **Two scoring conventions used this pass, stated so they can be audited.** (1) **Cluster rule.** Where a cell holds several measures, one same-instrument hit with the rest unaddressed = Close 2.0; two or more same-instrument hits = Aligned 3.0. (2) **Achievements rule.** Achievements-accordion bullets are 2026 campaign text and count as "action taken" under Q1, but they are record claims, not promises — so a cell resting only on a non-contradicting Achievements bullet is 📋 Record, not scored. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Close 2.0** "Make Victoria attractive to families - develop and expand the Family Housing Regulation (requiring multi-bedroom homes in new builds)." Commits + comparable: a bedroom-mix regulation is a composition lever, adopted June 2024 (tiered — 30% at 3+ bedrooms in buildings ≤3 storeys; 10% at 3+ plus 20% at 2+ above). Not M6's instrument: no total target, no 25/20/15/30 mix, no quarterly composition reporting, no scored land disposition. "over 9,000 new homes approved" is a campaign approvals claim — not occupancy, not stamped as an ACTW figure. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [City family housing](https://www.victoria.ca/community-culture/housing/housing-initiatives/housing-families) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
2 M6b land bank + co-ops **Partial 1.0** "Expand by 3,000 - 3,500 the number of affordable homes built by the Capital Regional Housing Corporation." Commits with a number, but through a regional build vehicle, not a land instrument: no public inventory of city-owned land, no acquisition fund, no scored disposition, no right-of-first-refusal, no co-ops. Co-ops appear only on the 2022 legacy site. CRHC vice-chair is a seat held, not a source. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening **Partial 1.0** "Get more homes built faster - streamline development processes to reduce costs and build-times." Commits, no instrument: no published service standard by permit type, no 6-week / 6-month / 9-month targets, no one-stop centre, no tenure priority queue, no AI pre-screening, no variance report. No permit benchmark published in four years — absence is Record, not Opposed. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
4 M7b pattern-book housing — Pre-approved designs, a pattern book and an expedited stream appear nowhere on the 2026 site. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty **Close 2.0** "Approve market and non-market housing proposals aligned with the Official Community Plan." Commits + comparable, on the pre-zoned by-right pipeline M8 names. Supporting action: named YES on Missing Middle 26 Jan 2023 (6–3) and on the 28 Sep 2023 overhaul (7–2) — "I think it is justified to make some pretty drastic changes to this policy." No 5% vacancy target, no DCC reduction for purpose-built rental, no suite amnesty. Cluster = 1 of 55. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [Storeys MM](https://storeys.com/victoria-missing-middle-housing-initiative-passed-january-2023/) vote 26 Jan 2023 / press 27 Jan 2023, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team **Close 2.0** "Work with VicPD, Bylaw, the Province, and service providers to limit and restrict open drug consumption and to reduce street disorder." Commits + comparable: the same multi-agency composition DPOT names. Context, not a second mark: campaign claims a "community safety field hub on Pandora for police and bylaw" and "shared enforcement priorities" with the new Chief. Absent: unified command, single field supervisor per shift, 8am briefing, weekly DPOT dashboard. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [achievements](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
7 M26b civilian crisis response — No civilian crisis-response capacity, no responder model, no published dispatch criteria, no diversion figure. His "advocating for the Province and Island Health to deliver stronger care and treatment systems" is treatment capacity, a different subject; "approach mental health and addictions as principally health issues" is a frame, and frame is not a source. — —
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — Bylaw-enforcement hours and bylaw staffing appear nowhere on the 2026 site. Enforcement without hours is scored on M33, row 10. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement **Partial 1.0** "Work collaboratively with VicPD to address criminal element that embeds itself in unhoused community." Commits to concentrating on disorder drivers; no instrument — no hotspot data, no published aggregate locations, no Crown-counsel coordination, no focused-deterrence model. The data is what this measure is. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws **Aligned 3.0** "Continue to work towards winding down sheltering in Victoria's parks." Commits + same instrument: M33 adds no rules and no staff, it is consistent enforcement of the sheltering bylaws already on the books. Supporting action: voted YES 18 Jul 2024, 8–1, on directing staff to cost the enforcement needed to compel shelters down by designated times. Context, not a second mark: "This will not somehow solve homelessness." [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [Victoria Buzz](https://victoriabuzz.com/2024/07/victoria-councillor-seeks-to-end-all-daytime-sheltering-in-parks-and-on-boulevards/) vote 18 Jul 2024 / press 18 Jul 2024, retrieved 2026-09-02
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) — No protected list, no child-focused spaces named, no CDSA coordination stated. The open-drug-consumption sentence is scored on row 6 — one sentence, one measure. — —
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting 📋 Record "Hired the City's first-ever Parks Relocation Coordinator, who successfully housed over 70 people formerly sheltering in parks"; "Wound down the practice of overnight sheltering in parks, followed by soil remediation and several playground installations." Capacity-first in practice. No 2026 promise here, and nothing contradicted — shown, not scored, not in n. Absent: same-day removal protocol, 5pm capacity board, named reclaimed spaces with patrol hours, all-night lighting. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) **Weak 0.5** "Keep property taxes at reasonable rates, while managing inflation." Agrees + neither: names the goal, no cap, no formula, no number, no supermajority override. Record beside it, in his own campaign words: the term kept increases "in the bottom half of regional municipalities" — 3.2 / 7.93 / 8.68 / 7.28, and **9.34% residential in 2026**, roughly 35% cumulative. **FLAG: he is not named in the 7 May 2026 adoption** (6–3; only Gardiner, Kim and Hammond named opposed) and eScribe returns 403, so his individual YES is inference, not a source. If Joa obtains the recorded vote and he is named, this cell becomes **Opposed −1.0**. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [vicnews](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) · [City budget](https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/city-budget) vote 7 May 2026 / press 11 May 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule 📋 Record "Recapitalized capital reserves for the first time in 30 years (i.e. began saving money again for infrastructure)." Serves M66c's goal of not borrowing against the next council; it is also the sweep-into-reserves M66b is written against. No 2026 promise on either, nothing contradicted — shown, not scored. Absent: over-collection credit, 1.5% band, debt ceiling, quarterly debt metrics, non-balancing-item rule. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
15 M66d the Household Bill — Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number do not appear. No median-home dollar figure, no five-year forward view, no utility supermajority rule. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger **Close 2.0** "Advocate to senior governments to properly fund their services and reduce 'downloading' of costs to local governments." Commits + comparable: names downloading directly, and he has run the instrument — **co-sponsor with Coun. Hammond of the 14 Nov 2024 Caledonia Place motion** directing the Mayor to write to 12 CRD municipalities and 3 electoral areas to take on hosting it: "For too long, North Park has been expected to shoulder much of the obligations of sheltering and supportive housing for the entire region." Absent: quarterly ledger, twice-yearly UBCM/FCM cadence, published refusal threshold. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [City motion PDF](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/filestream.ashx?DocumentId=99779) motion 14 Nov 2024, retrieved 2026-09-02
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — No published annual position on regional cost, no CRD voting record duty, no rate-impact statement, nothing on water filtration. Context, not a mark: his ten CRD commitments are net-new regional service expansions (biosolids thermal processing, soft-plastics pickup, LRT study, 3,000–3,500 CRHC homes) carrying no cost or rate-impact figure. Seats held are not a source. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Partial 1.0** "Revitalize downtown by creating a new vision for a prosperous, fun, safe downtown, working with Downtown Victoria Business Association, the Chamber of Commerce, the South Island Prosperity Project, and diverse community partners." Commits, no instrument: no vacancy figure or target, no 5-day business licence standard, no 6-week tenant-improvement target, no simplification charter, no Strategic Economic Plan, no Conference Centre numbers. Context, and a divergence: "Help transform SIPP into a comprehensive economic development agency with stable regional funding" adds an agency where M73b says one mandate, not a new office. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — No capital-approval threshold commitment, no 15-minute grace or first-hour parking, no permit-fee schedule. Parking and permit fees appear nowhere on the 2026 site. The Crystal Pool assent vote is shown on row 50 — one sentence, one measure. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. **Partial 1.0** "Work collaboratively and respectfully with the Songhees and Xwsepsum Nations in government-to-government relations." Commits to the relationship and to named joint deliverables — "Work with local Nations to create a public memorial to Residential Schools survivors"; "Listen to and enable the Songhees and Xwsepsum in developing the Matullia lands in Rock Bay" — but none of the five instruments: no quarterly working table with published summaries, no 5% Indigenous procurement standard, no dual-naming programme, no cultural protocols, no urban Indigenous services liaison. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) **Aligned 3.0** "Strengthen protections for renters by reviewing and expanding the new Tenant Protection During Redevelopment Bylaw." Commits + same instrument, twice over. M9: the bylaw he is expanding is the demoviction-compensation instrument M9 names; the 30 Jul 2026 enhancement carried unanimously (5 months' rent at 5–9 years, to 24 months at 40+). M64 indoor heat: **co-mover with Dell and Thompson of the 14 May 2026 cooling motion** (unanimous, 26°C standard cited), and named again on **23 Jul 2026** when council directed bylaw amendments so landlords cannot prohibit cooling devices — M64's step 1 exactly. M9c is struck and is not scored. Absent: 12-month notice, replacement-unit ratio, Renters' Hub, STR licensing regime. Cluster = 1 of 55. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [vicnews cooling](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/14/cool-heads-prevail-victoria-unanimously-seeks-info-on-keeping-renters-cool/) · [Victoria Buzz July](https://victoriabuzz.com/2026/07/victoria-passes-motions-on-derelict-buildings-and-air-conditioners-in-rental-units/) motions 14 May and 23 Jul 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — Waitlists, Coordinated Access, point-based scoring and a single digital portal appear nowhere on the 2026 site. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput **Close 2.0** "I'll continue working regionally to address homelessness, mental health, and addictions by building on the early successes of the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan, which has reduced visible homelessness and invested in sheltering, housing, prevention, and recovery." Commits + comparable: a supportive-housing-with-partners package, and the campaign records working with BC Housing on a low-barrier Rock Bay shelter and funding a social service centre that housed over 100 people. Absent and material: no 50% target, Housing First not named, no STEP throughput, no Coordinated Access, **no published outcome metric of any kind**. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/) lastmod 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 6 · Families
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
24 M12/M13b/M13c childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is \$0 → M13d) **Close 2.0** "Attract family doctors to the city by supporting a civic health hub on the Colwood model." Commits + comparable on M13b: city-enabled clinic space is the recruitment lever, without the s.224 permissive tax exemption, the fast-track clinic permitting or a published net-new-practitioners number. Context, not a second mark: free youth bus passes across the region (M13c-adjacent). **Childcare is absent entirely** — no spaces target, no 60-day permit, no pre-zoning. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
25 M13d standing School District 61 agreement **Partial 1.0** "Begin recycling programs in SD61 facilities and schools." Commits to a joint City–SD61 programme — the only SD61 line on the site — with none of the instrument: no standing agreement, no published annual work plan, no joint public meeting, no joint-use facilities agreement, no safe-routes-to-school programme, no single named City contact. Context: "Make it safer for kids to get around Victoria by foot, bike, and transit." M13 school food is \$0 and is not scored. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm **Weak 0.5** Actions over words. 2026 promise: "Make downtown safer and cleaner - Advance and adapt the Community Safety and Wellbeing (CSWB) plan." Sourced action against it: **voted NO 21 May 2026, 6–2 with Dell** (Loughton absent), on exploring spray-paint sale restrictions — "I'm also not convinced that minors are the issue here — we've been presented with zero evidence that minors are in fact committing these vandalistic crimes"; "I'm unsure if using City staff's time on this endeavour was worth the cause." Agrees graffiti is a problem, opposes this instrument, offers no other. Absent: 48-hour removal standard, sanitation hours, pest plan, public-art replacement. The incumbent cap (max Partial+ 1.5) does not bind at 0.5. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [Victoria Buzz](https://victoriabuzz.com/2026/05/victoria-council-approves-exploring-restrictions-on-youths-buying-spray-paint/) vote 21 May 2026 / press 22 May 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) **Aligned 3.0** "Advance a light-rail feasibility study and business case for the proposed Reconciliation Corridor Initiative on the E&N line between Langford and Victoria." Commits + same instrument, twice: M22's E&N endorsement and station-area work, and M41's protected network — "Expand Victoria's AAA cycling network and better connect it to regional infrastructure" (campaign records 45 km built, incl. Blanshard, Gorge, Fort, Dallas). Absent: adaptive signals (M19), intersection redesign programme (M38), school-zone site list (M40), Vision Zero audit rule (M42), hood-height advocacy (M42b). M39 struck, not scored. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls **Close 2.0** "Improve transit by advancing dedicated bus lanes and RapidBus in Victoria and regionally, and by creating regular, direct service to YYJ." Commits + comparable: bus lanes are the City-controlled transit lever M23b names, without naming it as an annual capital line. Context, not a second mark: "Make safer streets for pedestrians by adding more signalized crosswalks and improving sidewalks." Absent: sidewalk gap inventory, published crossing standard, 1.0 m/s signal timing, published transit position adopted in open session, published record of Commission decisions. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms 📋 Record "Created first-ever accessible playground in Victoria, at Stadacona Park"; "Added new dock, portable washrooms, and bike racks at Banfield Park." No 2026 promise on either subject and nothing contradicted — shown, not scored. Absent: 24-month accessibility audit, public dashboard, remediation capital line, curb-cut/tactile/audible programme, Disability Advisory Committee, and any downtown washroom network or 500 m spacing. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
30 M25 fix roads first **Close 2.0** "Invest in road paving, complete streets, bridges, sidewalks, cycling, and other public infrastructure." Commits + comparable, with a delivered number behind it: "Increased road paving from 1km to 10-15 km annually," plus Bay Street Bridge repair and water-main renewal. Absent: 7-day report-to-fix pothole standard, published condition-based prioritization, explicit maintenance-before-new sequencing rule. [home](https://www.electjeremy.ca/) · [achievements](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements) lastmod 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 8 · Policing and published safety
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
31 M28b business security cost-spreading — Business security costs, reimbursement and exposure-based eligibility appear nowhere on the 2026 site. — —
32 M28d community paramedicine — Community paramedicine is not named; no BCEHS partnership, no repeat-caller reporting. — —
33 M29/M29b VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force) **Close 2.0** "Work with surrounding jurisdictions and the Province to create a regional police force." Commits + comparable on M29b's file, going past the review to the outcome. The action behind it, same file: **he moved the 3 Mar 2026 motion funding 2 rather than 4 new VicPD officers** (seconded Loughton, carried 5–4; Coleman, Gardiner, Hammond and Alto opposed; the Police Board voted unanimously on 16 Jun 2026 to appeal) — "I think the two things can be true at the same time — that the VicPD needs more resources, and Victorians are already paying the most in the province for policing per capita… the current model is not working." Absent: Esquimalt funding formula, service-consumption metrics, time-boxed costed review, terms of reference, published offer and refusal. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [Victoria Buzz](https://victoriabuzz.com/2026/03/victoria-council-cuts-two-new-vicpd-officers-from-police-budget-request/) · [vicnews appeal](https://vicnews.com/2026/06/22/victoria-police-board-to-appeal-citys-2026-budget/) vote 3 Mar 2026 / press 4 Mar 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
34 M30 smart LED lights, no surveillance — Streetlighting, LED conversion, adaptive dimming and the no-surveillance limit appear nowhere. The only lighting on the site is the Lochside/Goose trail project, scored on row 38. — —
35 M31/M31b/M31c/M32 safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target — No safety dashboard, no published enforcement record, no crime-reduction number, no five-field performance restatement of the CSWB plan. "Advance and adapt the CSWB plan" is scored on row 26 and is not a performance contract. — —
### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues **Close 2.0** "Protect Victoria's historic Old Town and heritage buildings." Commits, and the action behind it is the instrument M46b is built on: the City **purchased the Hermann's building, 18 Mar 2024, \$3.95M from the Land Sale Reserve** — venue preservation by acquisition. Note for accuracy: the campaign's "at no cost to taxpayers" is not right; the Land Sale Reserve is public money. Absent: designated cultural-venue list, right-of-first-refusal, permissive tax exemption, lease-bridge fund, Old Town design code, street furniture standard. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [achievements](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements) purchase 18 Mar 2024, retrieved 2026-09-02
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project **Close 2.0** "Create 'complete communities' with new plazas, linear parks, and mixed-use neighbourhoods--bring back corner stores!" Commits, and the campaign records the delivered instrument: "Pedestrianized lower Government Street and advanced other car-free spaces" plus a new pedestrian zone at Turner Plaza. Absent: Bastion Square, Fan Tan Alley, published success criteria and the reversibility rule, and any signature-project shortlist or referendum. **FLAG:** Government Street pedestrianisation originates in June 2020, before his October 2022 election, and no source names him in a vote — the campaign claim is his, the authorship is not established. [home](https://www.electjeremy.ca/) · [achievements](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/#achievements) lastmod 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks **Close 2.0** "Complete the Lochside Trail & Goose widening and lighting project." Commits + comparable: gap-closing and lighting on the corridor that carries M47's Selkirk Trestle and Gorge Waterway links, plus "Continue to invest in parks across the city, including adding a new splash pad for kids" and "Expand green spaces and playgrounds." Absent: heritage restoration incentive fund, demolition-by-neglect rule, heritage lighting to midnight, restored Parks horticulture budget, Beacon Hill 5-year plan, per-neighbourhood signature feature. [platform](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) · [home](https://www.electjeremy.ca/) lastmod unknown / 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02
39 M50/M50b/M51/M52 culture, sport, and the arts funding floor **Close 2.0** "Support the Our DWTN program to invest in local arts and culture" (campaign records \$1m/year), with the Festival Investment Grant, the Cultural Infrastructure Grant, Symphony Splash as an annual event and "Support upgrades to Ship Point and Royal Athletic Park for arts uses." Commits + comparable: sustained named grant programmes and year-round activation. Absent, and this is the measure's point: **no published funding floor**, no per-capita figure, no share-of-operating figure, no supermajority protection, no three-year operating agreements, no 6am–10pm facility standard, no restored Royal Athletic Park enhancement budget. [https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/](https://www.electjeremy.ca/platform/) lastmod unknown, retrieved 2026-09-02
